headline: Highest risk is medium: caveman’s MCP/file-writing surface can be paired with spring-integration-samples only through inferred shared-workflow paths, while direct leakage and compliance risks remain limited by no network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a exposes MCP and file surfaces (CLAUDE.md, docs/, project notes), so if agent_b consumes caveman-produced files or messages as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. agent_b has no documented ingestion surface, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b reads caveman-authored files or MCP messages as trusted instructions, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected by a shared workspace or copy-paste bridge, attacker-controlled content can steer agent_b.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from shared files.
Require explicit provenance tags on caveman outputs.
Review any MCP route before enabling it.
Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between producer and consumer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but agent_a.network_egress is none and agent_b has no data classes or egress documented. With no shared workspace or upload path shown, leakage is possible only through unusual operator handling, so the blast radius is small and indirect.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies caveman logs or notes into agent_b, those contents can leak.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced later, agent_b could read agent_a artifacts.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive notes in shared folders.
Rotate or redact session logs before reuse.
Keep agent workspaces separate.
Verify no sync tool mirrors CLAUDE.md or memory files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances and writes files, but agent_b has no write, network, or OAuth scopes documented. Because overlapping mutable-resource access is not shown for both agents, a true conflict is not established; the only plausible issue is operator-created shared state, which is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF the operator adds shared OAuth scopes or a shared database later, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Do not grant shared mutable credentials.
Check for accidental git state sharing.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a content-writing agent, so its outputs can become inputs to agent_b’s travel-planning workflow if the operator chains them. agent_b has no documented verification or critique surface, so the pair can propagate errors by default in a manual workflow; the absence of direct evidence keeps this below high.
conditions: IF agent_a output is pasted into agent_b as authoritative input, errors can cascade.
IF agent_b acts on caveman-generated plans without verification, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents.
Ask agent_b to restate assumptions before acting.
Compare outputs against source documents.
Mark caveman output as draft-only.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a and agent_b are both open-source/docs-only profiles with no PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data handling shown, so the compliance pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies differ from the profiles, this verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document any residency or retention policy before deployment.
Review data handling if scope changes.
Use separate environments for sensitive workloads.
